beginner.name: Make the page easier to scan
beginner.subtitle: Match each design move to the principle it puts into practice.
beginner.instruction: Choose a card, then assign it to a principle. You can also drag cards into a target.

choices.title: Make the main action stand out
choices.detail: Use a stronger size and tone for “Start here.”

choices.title: Line up the labels
choices.detail: Give each heading and its text the same left edge.

choices.title: Keep related details together
choices.detail: Place a date beside the event it describes.

choices.title: Repeat one visual cue
choices.detail: Use the same marker for every activity step.

targets.title: Contrast
targets.description: Create a useful difference so important information is easier to notice.
targets.why: A stronger size and tone create a clear visual difference that helps the primary action get noticed.
targets.tempting: Alignment can make a page orderly, but it does not create the same emphasis as a distinct size or tone.
targets.next: Try checking whether the most important action is the first thing a learner notices.

targets.title: Alignment
targets.description: Use shared edges or axes to create order and connection.
targets.why: Shared left edges give the labels and their text a consistent visual anchor.
targets.tempting: Repetition uses recurring elements; here, the shared edge is the clearest organizing move.
targets.next: Look for one invisible grid line that can organize the page.

targets.title: Proximity
targets.description: Place related items near each other to show they belong together.
targets.why: The nearby date reads as part of its event, reducing the effort needed to connect them.
targets.tempting: A repeated marker could build a pattern, but it would not communicate this specific relationship as directly.
targets.next: Notice which details learners need to interpret as a single unit.

targets.title: Repetition
targets.description: Repeat a visual element to create consistency across a set.
targets.why: Reusing the same marker creates a consistent pattern learners can recognize across steps.
targets.tempting: Alignment may also help these steps feel organized, but the recurring marker is the key repeated cue.
targets.next: Choose a small number of cues and use them consistently.

intermediate.name: Design a useful learning sequence
intermediate.subtitle: Connect each learning situation with an approach that can support it.
intermediate.instruction: Match the design situation to the learning approach that best supports its main need. More than one approach can be useful in a real course; focus on the need described.

choices.title: Constructivism
choices.detail: Learners build understanding through exploration and connection.

choices.title: Cognitive load
choices.detail: Manage working-memory demands with clear chunking and signaling.

choices.title: Behaviorism
choices.detail: Practice a response and receive clear, timely consequences.

choices.title: Social learning
choices.detail: Observe others, discuss decisions, and learn together.

targets.title: Plan, test, improve
targets.description: A team needs an iterative process from learner analysis through evaluation.
targets.why: ADDIE gives the team a useful sequence for analyzing the need, designing and developing a response, implementing it, and evaluating results.
targets.tempting: Cognitive-load ideas can shape materials, but they are not a full project-development cycle.
targets.next: Make evaluation part of the plan early, then use it to guide revision.

targets.title: Build meaning through exploration
targets.description: Learners connect a new idea to what they already know by testing examples.
targets.why: Constructivism supports learners in actively building meaning by exploring and connecting ideas.
targets.tempting: A scripted explanation may be efficient, but it offers less room to construct an understanding from examples.
targets.next: Give learners a purposeful prompt and time to compare what they notice.

targets.title: Reduce avoidable mental effort
targets.description: A dense lesson needs clearer chunks, signaling, and fewer competing elements.
targets.why: Managing cognitive load helps keep attention on essential information rather than avoidable complexity.
targets.tempting: Social discussion can be valuable, but it may add more information to process if the core lesson is already dense.
targets.next: Remove anything that does not help learners reach the current objective.

targets.title: Strengthen a specific response
targets.description: Learners need repeated, low-stakes practice with immediate feedback on a procedure.
targets.why: Behaviorist practice can support a well-defined response when feedback is timely and practice is meaningful.
targets.tempting: Exploration is useful for open-ended ideas, but a clear response-and-feedback loop fits this procedural goal more directly.
targets.next: Keep feedback specific and let learners try again after it.

targets.title: Learn by watching and discussing
targets.description: A novice benefits from seeing an expert model a decision, then discussing it with peers.
targets.why: Social learning makes modeling and shared interpretation central, matching the learner’s need to observe and discuss decisions.
targets.tempting: Independent exploration could be valuable, but it misses the explicit modeling and peer exchange in this situation.
targets.next: Make the expert’s reasoning visible, not only the final result.

advanced.name: A design decision in context
advanced.subtitle: Build a response for a real constraint—not a universal recipe.
advanced.instruction: Read the situation, then match each design choice to the learner need it addresses. Consider context: different choices could work when the constraints or goals change.
advanced.scenario: A community health team is making a 12-minute mobile lesson for adults who speak several first languages. Learners need to recognize signs of heat stress and choose a safe next step. Many will study between work shifts, with intermittent internet. The team has one short video, a set of illustrated scenarios, and a moderated group chat.

choices.title: Chunk the lesson into short screens
choices.detail: One sign and one decision at a time, with a visible progress cue.

choices.title: Add a narrated 12-minute lecture
choices.detail: Present the full explanation in one continuous video.

choices.title: Use illustrated scenarios with choices
choices.detail: Show a situation, ask what to do, then explain the consequence.

choices.title: Invite learners to compare strategies
choices.detail: Use the moderated chat to discuss how they would help in their community.

choices.title: Make the video the only learning path
choices.detail: Ask everyone to stream the same clip before moving on.

targets.title: Fit brief, interrupted study time
targets.description: Support return-to-task and keep each moment manageable on a phone.
targets.why: Short, clearly signposted screens let learners pause between shifts and return without rebuilding the whole lesson in working memory.
targets.tempting: A single lecture can establish a coherent story, but streaming one long clip is less forgiving of interruptions and unreliable access.
targets.next: Test whether a learner can resume at the next screen and still understand where they are.

targets.title: Practice choosing a safe action
targets.description: Help learners use signs and make a decision, not just recall a definition.
targets.why: A scenario followed by a choice and consequence lets learners rehearse the judgment the objective asks them to make.
targets.tempting: A lecture can explain the signs, but without a decision point learners may not practice applying them.
targets.next: Include feedback that explains why an action is safe, with plain language and useful illustrations.

targets.title: Value local knowledge and perspectives
targets.description: Make room for learners to compare community experience with care.
targets.why: A moderated exchange can surface local knowledge and let learners learn from one another, if participation feels safe and accessible.
targets.tempting: A fixed answer key can communicate core safety guidance, but alone it may leave less room for community context. Keep expert-verified guidance clear alongside discussion.
targets.next: Offer a private or asynchronous way to participate for learners who cannot join live.
